title: The Law That Made Margarine Pink
topic: Why one state demanded pink margarine
mechanism: New Hampshire allowed margarine to be sold only if it was dyed pink, and the Supreme Court ruled in 1898 that a permission tied to a condition nobody would buy is really a ban.

beats.hook: He sold one ten-pound tub of margarine and a stamp slams down: FINED $100. Not for the taste, for the colour.
beats.story: A margarine seller in an 1890s New Hampshire general store; his margarine looks and is dyed just like butter.
beats.rise: The state law looks friendly: sell as much as you like, just print OLEOMARGARINE in half-inch letters. He does, and it feels like easy money.
beats.twist: The shop door opens: a lawman walks in, opens the law book on the counter and reads the last line: UNLESS IT IS PINK.
beats.mechanism: Pink dye vat (PINK DYE), breakfast customer refusing it, fine ticket $100, jail calendar 60 DAYS, Supreme Court bench with docket card 1898, colour cards NATURAL / NOT PINK, stamp UNSELLABLE, a padlocked door SALES OPEN with a padlock PINK, sign PERMIT flipping to BAN, tubs dyed BLUE / RED / BLACK, a STINK tub, two DISSENT cards, the fine stamped REVERSED.
beats.ending: Back in the store a new seller gets a YES from the law book, a pink paint bucket lands on his tub, and the last card says NO.
